parsed.headline: Iranian army spokesperson says armed forces are prepared for potential U.S. attacks

pages.text: Iranian army spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia stated on Sunday that Iranian armed forces are fully prepared for any new attacks from the United States. Akraminia warned that the United States would suffer greater damage following comments from U.S. President Donald Trump, who said he had rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the fighting. The report was provided by the North Press Agency.

parsed.headline: CSIR to host Scientific Conference and Innovation Fair 2026 in October

pages.text: The Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) plans to convene scientists, businesses, investors, and policymakers in October to facilitate the transition of locally developed research into market-ready products, new businesses, and solutions for development challenges in Ghana. According to CSIR Director-General Prof. Paul Bosu, the CSIR Scientific Conference and Innovation Fair 2026 will showcase research spanning agriculture, food security, biotechnology, construction, water resources, environmental protection, and industrial development. During a media launch, Bosu announced that the Scientific Conference is scheduled to run from October 14 to 15, followed by the Innovation Fair from October 16 to 18. He stated the conference is intended to provide a platform for researchers to generate, share, and examine knowledge, while the fair aims to move findings toward practical use, adoption, and commercialization. Bosu noted the initiative is intended to strengthen links between research institutions and Ghana’s productive sectors. Additionally, Deputy Director-General of CSIR Prof. Marian Dorcas Quain disclosed that more than 500 scientists across the council’s 13 institutes are currently conducting over 300 research projects valued at nearly GH¢100 million.

parsed.headline: United States and China agree to establish AI and military crisis communication channels

pages.text: Following a three-day summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, the United States and China agreed on Saturday to establish a channel for handling artificial intelligence-related incidents and to accelerate work on military crisis communications. China’s Foreign Ministry stated that the two sides would sign a memorandum of understanding intended to strengthen crisis communications and assist in preventing crises between their militaries, though the ministry provided few details regarding the agreement. Additionally, the countries will establish a mechanism to discuss the risks and benefits of AI, with a dedicated dialogue scheduled for November. Analysts noted that while the summit produced no major breakthroughs on longstanding differences, these new working-level mechanisms could help prevent tensions from escalating. Wang Zichen of the Center for China and Globalization commented that the emphasis on military dialogue and crisis-management mechanisms highlighted the importance of personal diplomacy between the two leaders.

parsed.headline: Flood emergency declared in Bangkok as heavy rains submerge roads

pages.text: A flood emergency disaster has been declared across all 50 districts of Bangkok after more than 300mm (12in) of rain fell since September 24, 2026. The rainfall has left roads in the Thai capital submerged and inundated the city's drainage system. On Saturday, Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt reported that the east of the city had been hardest hit, according to AFP. While the Bangkok Metropolitan Authority stated on Sunday that rains have subsided, canal water levels remain high. No casualties have been reported in Bangkok from this flooding event. Residents living near the city's network of canals have been advised to move belongings to upper floors, and people have been urged to stay at home. Somkid Pheuk-ngam, a resident living near a canal north of central Bangkok, told AFP that water had reached waist level at her location. The Thai Meteorological Service has forecast more heavy rain through the week, though the area of low pressure causing recent downpours is expected to move towards central Thailand.

parsed.headline: Syria expects over $1 billion in foreign capital for new banks

pages.text: Central Bank of Syria Governor Mohammad Safwat Raslan stated that foreign capital flowing into Syria to establish new banks is expected to exceed $1 billion in the coming period. Speaking to Syria’s state-run news agency (SANA), Raslan noted that Jordanian banks have submitted applications to invest in Syria, while existing Jordanian banks in the country are seeking to increase their investments. Licensing for Islamic and conventional banks remains subject to regulatory standards, including applicants' reputation, experience, and financial solvency, alongside a requirement for a strategic banking partner to hold at least a 10 percent stake in a new bank. Under new legislation, foreign investors are permitted to retain up to 60 percent of paid-up capital in foreign currency, with guarantees for profit transfers and the removal of restrictions on the buying, selling, and transferring of foreign currency.

Raslan indicated that the Central Bank plans to require financial institutions providing international money-transfer services to deliver remittances to beneficiaries exclusively in foreign currency. He encouraged international money-transfer companies and service providers to enter the Syrian market via local financial institutions to open secure transfer channels. Regarding infrastructure, Raslan said most Syrian banks have begun providing electronic compliance and monitoring tools to meet Financial Action Task Force (FATF) requirements and connect with the SWIFT system. Additionally, he mentioned a plan to use Arab currencies pegged to the U.S. dollar to settle imports and exports to facilitate trade between Syria and relevant Arab nations.

parsed.headline: Neskantaga First Nation chiefs seek regional support amid ongoing evacuation

pages.text: During the Nishnawbe Aski Nation (NAN) annual Keewaywin Conference this week, Neskantaga’s former chief Wayne Moonias appealed to regional chiefs for support as the community continues to deal with an ongoing evacuation. Neskantaga First Nation, an Ojibway community located approximately 440 kilometres northeast of Thunder Bay, Ontario, declared a state of emergency on Aug. 4 following a sewage spill at its nursing station, which serves as the community's only health-care facility. More than 250 people from the community of fewer than 400 were evacuated to a hotel in Toronto and remain there nearly eight weeks later. Remediation work on the damaged nursing station has only recently begun. Chief Gary Quisses told CBC News that it could be a month or more before the nursing station reopens, noting that the timeline may change due to approaching cold weather and snow. This follows a period of instability at the facility, including a small fire caused by a space heater a few weeks ago. A temporary nursing station has been established in the community, though Chief Quisses stated the space lacks privacy and is limited to providing basic care such as bandages and painkillers. This is the second time issues at the health-care facility have prompted an evacuation; last year, community members were displaced for three months due to a flood and the smell of fuel in the building. Neskantaga is one of 49 First Nations represented by NAN across treaties 9 and 5.

parsed.headline: Tensions rise in the Strait of Hormuz following rejection of diplomatic solution

pages.text: Following US President Donald Trump's rejection of a diplomatic solution proposed by Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian media reported hearing explosions in the waterway. Reports of blasts near southern Iran’s Qeshm Island suggested that multiple antiship missiles and drones were fired at vessels transiting the waterway against Tehran’s wishes, though Iranian authorities did not confirm any attacks on that day. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) maintains that the strait is closed to any ship that does not coordinate with Iranian authorities. On Sunday afternoon, the IRGC released video of what it said was a second US underwater drone seized this month. While Iranian authorities have not confirmed specific attacks on that day, shipping continues to face attacks in the waters, including an incident last week involving an Indian cargo ship that killed a sailor. Tehran has stated the strait will not fully reopen until the US blockade on Iranian ports ends, and has issued instructions for shipping companies to use a temporary route approved by Iranian authorities and pay relevant fees. On September 26, 2026, Iran’s Persian Gulf Strait Authority announced it would blacklist any shipping charterer company that orders crews to use routes it considers unauthorized. The authority also published what it described as an apology from an unnamed shipowner who blamed commercial pressure from a charterer for attempting to pass through the strait. Washington maintains that its warships are successfully guiding oil tankers out of the strait via a different route. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told Fox News on Sunday that the running average of crude oil in transit was nearly 13 million barrels per day.

parsed.headline: President Mahama announces plans for 1,200MW state-owned gas power plant in Ghana

pages.text: During a town hall meeting with the Ghanaian community in New York on September 25, 2026, President John Dramani Mahama announced plans for Ghana to build a 1,200-megawatt (MW) state-owned gas-fired thermal power plant. The President stated that the government intends to sign an agreement for the project before the end of 2026. If completed as planned, the facility would have a higher installed capacity than the 1,020MW Akosombo Hydroelectric Power Station, which is currently Ghana's largest single generating facility by installed capacity.

Mr. Mahama said the decision to add the new thermal capacity was informed by changes in the global energy landscape, including the transition toward renewable energy and the growing adoption of electric vehicles. He noted that the government wants to avoid investing in power assets that could become stranded as the energy mix changes. While the President stated that some Independent Power Producers (IPPs) are prepared to invest in an additional 500MW of capacity, he said the government would prefer to develop additional state-owned generation capacity.

President Mahama also stated that the government has cleared energy sector debts and reorganized the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) to prioritize payments to power producers, which he said has helped stabilize electricity supply. He noted that while IPPs had previously threatened to suspend power generation, the government is now current with payments.

parsed.headline: Iran seeks to shift oil exports and goods imports to Caspian Sea amid southern port blockade

pages.text: Tehran is making adjustments to export oil and import essential goods as its southern ports face a United States naval blockade, according to Al Jazeera. This shift comes as no breakthrough has been reached to end the war launched by the United States and Israel on Iran on February 28. Recent United Nations efforts to resolve the deadlock between Iran and the U.S. appear to have failed following U.S. President Donald Trump's statement that Tehran’s offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz was unacceptable. The Caspian Sea, located on Iran’s northern coast and shared by Iran, Russia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, and Turkmenistan, is being viewed as a potential portal for trade.

Experts noted that maritime trade via the Caspian Sea faces logistical challenges due to declining water levels. In April, UN Environment Programme Executive Director Inger Andersen stated that Caspian water levels had dropped by approximately 2 metres (6.6ft) since the 1990s. Shahram Fadakar, director general of the Iranian Department of Environment’s Office for Coastal and Marine Ecosystem Protection, told local media last week that water levels have been dropping by more than 20cm (7.9 inches) annually over the past two to three years. Projections suggest sea levels could recede by an additional 8 to 21 metres (26ft to 69ft) by the end of the century, a trend that could affect trade between all Caspian countries, including Iran.

parsed.headline: Germany and Syria begin talks regarding the return of Syrian migrants

pages.text: Germany and Syria have entered talks concerning the return of Syrians living in Germany, according to German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt. Speaking to Rudaw on September 26, 2026, Dobrindt stated that while a process has been embarked upon following Syrian Transitional President Ahmad al-Sharaa’s visit to Germany, the two countries have not yet reached a final agreement. These discussions follow recent meetings between officials, including a September 25 meeting in Damascus where a German Interior Ministry delegation met with Syrian officials to discuss refugee returns and reintegration. According to Syrian state media, German officials emphasized that returns should be voluntary, dignified, and coordinated with Syrian authorities.

Dobrindt indicated that German authorities are considering three distinct groups of Syrians in this process. The first group includes individuals convicted of serious crimes, whose return Berlin intends to pursue quickly. The second group consists of people without a clear legal basis to remain in Germany, while the third group includes those who have integrated into German society, hold jobs, and have prospects of staying. Germany is considering both deportations and incentives for voluntary returns. The German government reports it has hosted more than one million Syrians who fled the war that began in 2011, and Berlin has also begun reviewing the protection status of some Syrians.
